brief.subject: Social Security wage cap rises to $192,300 for 2027
brief.headline: Payroll Tax Cap Climbs to $192,300 in 2027; IRS Finalizes Direct Card Payment Rules
brief.dek: The 2027 Social Security wage base rises, the IRS can take card payments directly, and dyed diesel penalties are paused through 2026.
brief.lede: The Social Security payroll tax cap rises from $184,500 to $192,300 in 2027. Update payroll setups and estimated tax plans before year-end.

sections.heading: Social Security wage base goes up
bullets: The payroll tax cap moves from $184,500 to $192,300 in 2027, so more high-end wages face Social Security tax.
Employers paying salaries above the old cap should update payroll systems before the first 2027 pay run.
Self-employed owners with large net earnings will owe Social Security tax on more income next year.
Benefits also get a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment, according to the Social Security Administration.

sections.heading: IRS can take cards directly
bullets: Final IRS rules let the agency accept credit and debit card tax payments itself, without routing taxpayers to outside processors.
The rules implement Taxpayer First Act changes and lift limits on the IRS paying fees under card-payment contracts.
Card payment terms could change, so check costs before charging your next tax bill.

sections.heading: Dyed diesel penalties paused
bullets: The IRS is suspending federal tax penalties for selling or using dyed diesel on highways nationwide for the rest of 2026.
Trucking, farming and construction businesses gain temporary relief from a normally costly violation.

sections.heading: Premium tax credit rules proposed
bullets: Proposed IRS regulations would change premium tax credit eligibility, how the credit is computed, and repayment of excess advance credits.
Freelancers buying Exchange health coverage should watch for changes that could affect their year-end tax bill.

brief.seo_description: 2027 Social Security wage cap rises to $192,300, IRS finalizes direct card payment rules, and dyed diesel penalties are paused for 2026.

items.title: Rule: Regulations Regarding Payment of Tax by Commercially Acceptable Means
items.snippet: This document contains final regulations regarding the payment of tax by commercially acceptable means. The final regulations reflect changes to the law made by the Taxpayer First Act that would allow the IRS to directly accept payments of tax by credit or debit card, without having to connect taxpayers to third-party payment processors. items.title: Social Security’s Payroll Tax Cap is Going Up in 2027
items.snippet: Along with a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment for retirees, people with disabilities and dependents, the Social Security Administration said the payroll tax cap will increase from $184,500 to $192,300.

items.title: Rule: Non-Applicability of Section 357(c) to Consolidated Groups
items.snippet: This document contains final regulations clarifying that, in the case of certain transfers between members of a consolidated group, a transferee's assumption of certain liabilities will not reduce the transferor's basis in the transferee's stock received in the transfer. These final regulations affect consolidated groups and their members.

items.title: IRS Halts Penalties for Dyed Diesel Fuel Use for the Rest of 2026
items.snippet: The IRS announced Wednesday evening that it's temporarily suspending federal tax penalties when dyed diesel fuel is sold for use or used on highways nationwide.
